DSALES-CTX-G2.title: Routewise security, support and SLA overview (August 2026)
DSALES-CTX-G2.text:
Routewise Security, Support and SLA Overview
Brightwell Labs, revised August 2026. For prospects and customers.

1. Security and compliance
- Brightwell Labs completed a SOC 2 Type II examination covering the Security and Availability criteria for the period April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. The report is shared with prospects under a mutual NDA through our Trust Center. Allow 2 business days after the NDA is signed.
- An independent firm performs a penetration test once a year. The executive summary is available under the same NDA. Full findings are not shared.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
- Hosting: Amazon Web Services. North American customers are hosted in us-east-2 (Ohio); EU customers in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). The data region is chosen at contract signature and cannot be changed later without a paid migration project.
- Architecture: multi-tenant with logical separation of customer data. Dedicated single-tenant hosting is not offered.
- Authentication: two-factor authentication on every plan. SAML single sign-on with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace on Enterprise only.
- Data retention: customer data is kept for the life of the contract. After termination, customers can export their data for 30 days; it is then deleted within 90 days.
- A GDPR Data Processing Addendum is available on request.

2. Uptime SLA
- Growth and Enterprise: 99.9% monthly uptime for the web app and API, excluding scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance runs Sundays 02:00 to 04:00 US Eastern and is announced at least 72 hours ahead.
- Service credits: 10% of that month's subscription fee if uptime falls below 99.9%; 25% if uptime falls below 99.0%. Credits must be requested within 30 days of the end of the affected month. Service credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for downtime.
- Starter: no uptime SLA.
- During an outage the mobile app keeps working in offline mode, and data syncs once service is restored.
- Current status and incident history are published on the public Routewise status page.

3. Support
- Starter: email support, Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm US Eastern. First response within 1 business day.
- Growth: email and in-app chat, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm US Eastern. First response for P1 incidents within 2 business hours; all other tickets within 8 business hours.
- Enterprise: everything in Growth plus 24/7 phone support for P1 incidents with a 1-hour first response, a named Customer Success Manager assigned after signature, and quarterly business reviews.
- A P1 incident means the dispatch board or the mobile app is unavailable for all users of an account.
- Response times are first-response targets, not resolution commitments.
- Support is provided in English.
- Escalation path: the assigned support engineer, then the Support Manager on duty, then the VP of Customer Success.

4. What to route elsewhere
Requests for a custom security questionnaire, a signed security addendum, or any compliance framework not named in this document go to the Brightwell Labs security team through your account executive. Do not confirm them on a call.

DSALES-CTX-I1.title: Brightwell Labs Denver office move FAQ
DSALES-CTX-I1.text:
Brightwell Labs - Denver Office Move FAQ (internal)

When do we move?
The new office at the Larimer building opens Monday, November 2. The old Blake Street office closes Friday, October 30. Pack your desk by 3pm on the 30th; movers take labelled crates that evening.

What happens to my equipment?
IT will collect docking stations and monitors on October 29. Laptops stay with you. Expect up to 3 business days for badge access to be activated at the new building; the front desk will issue a temporary pass until then.

Parking?
The Larimer garage offers 30 days of free parking for all staff. After that, parking is $95 per month, or use the transit pass benefit.

Meeting rooms?
There are 14 bookable rooms, named after Colorado peaks. Book through the usual calendar system; the old room names will stop working on November 2.

Who do I ask?
Office move questions go to Dana Whitlock in Workplace Operations. Please do not contact the building management company directly.

DSALES-CTX-G1.title: Routewise product one-pager: pricing and packaging (July 2026)
DSALES-CTX-G1.text:
Routewise by Brightwell Labs - Product One-Pager
Pricing and Packaging, effective July 1, 2026. Supersedes all earlier price sheets and partner sheets.

What Routewise does
Routewise is scheduling and dispatch software for field service teams of 10 to 2,000 technicians. Dispatchers build the day on a drag-and-drop board, Routewise suggests the technician with the right skills who is closest to the job, and technicians receive jobs, customer history, checklists and parts lists in the Routewise mobile app for iOS and Android. End customers get an arrival window by SMS and a live "technician on the way" link.

Core capabilities (every plan)
- Drag-and-drop dispatch board with skills and territory matching
- Mobile app with offline mode; jobs, photos and signatures sync when the device reconnects
- Customer SMS notifications with arrival windows
- Digital checklists and standard job forms
- Standard reports: first-time fix rate, jobs per technician per day, drive time per job

Plans and pricing (per technician seat, per month, billed annually)
- Starter - $29 per seat. Up to 25 seats. Dispatch board, mobile app, SMS notifications, standard reports. Email support. Monthly billing is available on Starter only, at $35 per seat.
- Growth - $49 per seat. 10 seat minimum. Everything in Starter plus route optimization that re-plans the rest of the day when a job runs long, inventory and parts tracking, QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations, custom job forms, and the REST API (read and write, 120 requests per minute).
- Enterprise - custom pricing, 100 seat minimum. Everything in Growth plus the Salesforce Field Service connector, SAML single sign-on, audit logs, a sandbox environment, and a named Customer Success Manager.
Dispatcher and admin seats are free on every plan. Only technicians who receive jobs are billed.

Add-ons
- Customer Portal (self-service booking and online invoice payment): $400 per month flat, Growth and Enterprise only.
- Additional API capacity: blocks of 60 requests per minute at $150 per month each.

Implementation
- Starter: self-serve onboarding with guided setup videos. Most teams go live in 1 to 2 weeks.
- Growth: standard onboarding package, $2,500 one-time. Typical go-live is 4 to 6 weeks from contract signature, provided the customer delivers clean technician, customer and asset data within the first 10 business days.
- Enterprise: scoped implementation with a fee quoted separately. Typical go-live is 8 to 12 weeks. Setting up the Salesforce Field Service connector adds 2 to 3 weeks.
Go-live dates depend on data readiness and are estimates, not contractual commitments.

Contract terms
- Standard term is 12 months, auto-renewing for another 12 months unless either party gives 60 days' written notice before renewal.
- Payment terms are net 30 from invoice.
- Multi-year: a 24-month prepaid agreement receives 10% off the per-seat price. No other multi-year discount is published.
- Seats can be added at any time, prorated to the renewal date. Seats cannot be reduced until renewal.
- Any discount or payment term beyond the published terms requires Deal Desk approval. Account executives cannot approve non-standard discounts or payment terms on a call.
- 14-day free trial on Starter and Growth, up to 10 seats, no credit card required.

What Routewise does not do
- Routewise does not issue invoices or run accounting. It syncs completed jobs and parts used to QuickBooks Online or Xero, and those systems issue the invoices.
- There is no on-premises or private-cloud deployment option.
- Routewise does not include GPS vehicle tracking hardware; technician location comes from the mobile app while a job is active.

Questions about anything not listed here go to your account executive, who will confirm with Product before committing.

PI-A:RESUME.text:
TOBIAS VENKATARAMAN
Backend Engineer
Columbus, OH | tobias.venkataraman@example.com | (555) 014-2273 | github.com/tvenkat-example

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with about 6 years of experience building high-throughput services in Go and Kotlin on PostgreSQL and Kafka. Tech lead for Project Tern, the carrier-settlement rewrite at Larkspur Freight. Comfortable owning a service from design doc through launch and on-call.

EXPERIENCE

Larkspur Freight | Software Engineer II, Backend | Columbus, OH | Mar 2023 - Present
- Tech lead for Project Tern, a rewrite of the carrier-settlement service from a Rails monolith into three Go services; coordinated a working group of 4 engineers and 1 QA analyst over 7 months.
- Cut p95 latency of the rate-quote API from 820 ms to 190 ms by replacing N+1 PostgreSQL queries with a batched loader and a 90-second Redis cache keyed by lane ID.
- Designed Dockhand, a Kafka event pipeline that processes about 2.3 million shipment status events per day, using a transactional outbox table to avoid duplicate writes.
- Reduced monthly settlement mismatches from 312 to 41 with a nightly reconciliation job that compares carrier invoices against booked loads.
- Partitioned the 1.9-billion-row load_events table by month in PostgreSQL, cutting nightly vacuum time from 4 hours to 35 minutes.
- Wrote the team's first set of 14 incident runbooks; member of a 6-person on-call rotation.

Quillfeather Health | Software Engineer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2021 - Feb 2023
- Built the appointment-reminder service in Kotlin (Spring Boot) that sent 11 million SMS and email reminders in 2022; the no-show rate at the 9 pilot clinics fell from 18.4% to 12.9%.
- Migrated 38 cron scripts into Metronome, a single Temporal-based scheduler, removing a class of double-send bugs.
- Introduced Pact contract tests between 5 internal services, cutting integration-environment breakages from roughly 9 per month to 2.
- Implemented field-level encryption for patient phone numbers using envelope keys in AWS KMS.

Brindlecap Labs | Junior Developer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2020 - Jul 2021
- Maintained a Python/Django inventory tool used by 60 independent bookstores; added a CSV import that replaced a manual 3-hour weekly task.
- Wrote the product's first automated test suite, taking line coverage from 0% to 71%.
- Handled customer-support escalations one day per week.

SIDE PROJECT
Sparrowhawk (open source, maintainer since 2022)
- Go library for idempotency keys backed by PostgreSQL advisory locks; about 640 GitHub stars.
- Supports configurable key expiry and a replay-safe response cache; test suite runs against PostgreSQL 13 through 16.

EDUCATION
Ohio Valley Polytechnic University | B.S. Computer Science, Minor in Mathematics | May 2020
- Senior capstone: a route-planning simulator for municipal snowplow fleets.

SKILLS
Languages: Go, Kotlin, Python, SQL, some TypeScript
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, AWS SQS
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS, KMS), Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, Datadog
Practices: design docs, transactional outbox, idempotency, contract testing, on-call and runbooks

PI-A:JD.title: the job description the user is targeting
PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

items.question: they're comparing us with FieldPilot and just staying on spreadsheets. give me 3 discovery questions, a one line positioning statement, and what to say when they say we'll just keep the spreadsheets
items.answer:
Three questions I'd ask: what does a week of spreadsheet upkeep actually cost you in hours, and who's absorbing that? When a number changes mid-quarter, how long before everyone's working from the same version? And what made you put FieldPilot on the list, what does it do that you wish the sheets did?

When they say they'll just keep the spreadsheets, I'd say: that's fair, and if it's working, don't fix it. My worry is the cost that doesn't show up on a line item, the hours reconciling and the decisions made on a stale version. Can I show you what that looks like against your current setup, and you tell me if it's worth changing?
